correction.text: "The AHP led to the widespread settlement of the Sahara and the Arabian Desert"; "People in the Sahara lived as hunter-gatherers and domesticated cattle, goats, and sheep"; the Sahara less Egypt (Nabta Playa, Nile cultures) and less the Capsian country (Tunisia, northern Algeria)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Sahara region of the gazetteer less Egypt and less the Capsian country (27,973 land cells, about 7.1 M km2). The African humid period page says the Sahara was widely settled but gives no dated extent: low confidence, drawn so that the Early Holocene Sahara is not left blank beside the dated sites of Nabta Playa (Egypt), Gobero (Niger) and the Acacus (Libya).

correction.text: the Sahara as in the first keyframe, less the Gobero disc held by the Tenerian from 5200 BCE

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe from 5200 BCE: the same Sahara less the 100 km Gobero disc (27,856 land cells), which the Tenerian culture holds from 5200 BCE (Gobero page: "Phase III dates from 5200 BCE to 2200 BCE").

region.text: "The AHP led to the widespread settlement of the Sahara and the Arabian Desert"; "People in the Sahara lived as hunter-gatherers and domesticated cattle, goats, and sheep"; the Sahara less Egypt (Nabta Playa, Nile cultures) and less the Capsian country (Tunisia, northern Algeria)

ledger.note: 6000 BCE (project floor): the Sahara is green and settled. "The AHP led to the widespread settlement of the Sahara and the Arabian Desert"; "People in the Sahara lived as hunter-gatherers and domesticated cattle, goats, and sheep" (no date given); the Acacus page: "The Acacus Mountains were occupied by hunter-gatherers continuously in the Holocene". The page gives no dated extent, so the whole Sahara region is a bridging judgment.

region.text: Gobero in the Ténéré desert of Niger, 100 km disc

ledger.note: 5200 BCE: the Tenerian settle Lake Gobero in the Ténéré. "Phase III dates from 5200 BCE to 2200 BCE", after "an interruption in the occupation of the site from 6200-5200 BCE". The disc is the dossier's stand-in for the Tenerian land.

5050 BCE: domestic animals reach the Acacus Mountains. "Animal domestication as part of the African Neolithic was introduced in this region by around 7000 BP"; milk lipids on ceramics "radiocarbon-dated to 7,500 BP". 7,000 BP is 5050 BCE; the page speaks of the Acacus (Libya), not of the whole Sahara.

region.text: the Sahara as in the first keyframe, less the Gobero disc held by the Tenerian from 5200 BCE

ledger.note: 3550 BCE: the Green Sahara ends. "The African humid period ended 6,000-5,000 years ago during the Piora Oscillation cold period"; "While some evidence points to an end 5,500 years ago in the Sahel, Arabia, and East Africa"; 5,500 BP is 3550 BCE. The page adds that "the end of the period appears to have occurred in several steps, such as the 4.2-kiloyear event". The land passes to nobody.

certainty.note: A whole desert with no recorded border; the extent is a placement.

sources.title: African humid period
sources.note: Humid period began about 14,600 years ago and ended 6,000-5,000 years ago (5,500 in the Sahel, Arabia and East Africa); the Sahara widely settled; regional Tchadien and Nouakchottien phases.

sources.title: Tadrart Acacus
sources.note: Acacus Mountains of Libya: hunter-gatherers continuously in the Holocene; animal domestication by around 7000 BP; Late Acacus 8870-7400 BP; rock art 12,000 BCE to 100 CE.

sources.title: Gobero
sources.note: Tenerian Phase III 5200-2200 BCE at Gobero, Ténéré desert, Niger.

sources.title: Pastoral Neolithic
sources.note: Opened and not used for any event: this is the East African Pastoral Neolithic (5000 BP - 1200 BP; Lake Turkana, Kenya and Tanzania), not the Saharan one; it records that domestic animals "reached Eastern Africa by 5000 BP" from northern Africa.

notes: Green Sahara cultures: the dossier that stands for "the Saharan cattle herders" of the brief across the whole desert outside Egypt, the Capsian country and the Gobero disc. It is a confidence-1 placement: the AHP page says the Sahara was widely settled without dating or mapping it. The dated sites are the separate dossiers nabta-playa-neolithic (Egypt, cattle morphologically wild), tenerian-culture (Niger) and the Acacus pastoralism date of this dossier's rename. The Wikipedia article titled Pastoral Neolithic is about Kenya and Tanzania (5000 BP onward) and starts after the 3400 BCE horizon; it was opened (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pastoral_Neolithic: "The Pastoral Neolithic (5000 BP - 1200 BP)", earliest sites at Lake Turkana) but no dossier was written for it (see the batch notes). The Sahel (Tichitt starts 2600 BCE) is left to tichitt-tradition. The end, 3550 BCE, is the AHP page's 5,500 BP; the page's range 6,000-5,000 BP is 4050-3050 BCE. Sudan's Nile (Khartoum) and Lower Nubia are separate dossiers; whether the gazetteer Sahara region touches them was checked with the gazetteer (no shared cell).
